Thanks for doing this, Marcelo. So, halfway through. Has it got easier?
I think so, but not in the way I expected. The more I speak, the less I notice my own progress.
Interesting. Was there a moment when you nearly gave up?
Yes. I was going to stop in July. Then I had my calls recorded and listened to them, and I could pinpoint three habits.
What is your sticking point now?
Under pressure, I fall back on simple sentences. Having seen that, I now practice the hard ones on purpose.
And what would you tell someone who is about to quit?
Do less, but do it every week. Consistency matters more than hours, and then you raise the bar.

Hi Marcelo, it is Fiona again. I hope the debate after my last column did not keep you up at night. I have a new idea, and I would love your help. My editor wants a piece on adults who learn a language in the middle of a busy career. Having interviewed three teachers already, I need one learner who is honest about it, not a success story. I was going to ask a friend of mine, but she has only just started, and I want someone who is halfway. Could you give me twenty minutes on Thursday? I want to know three things. What has changed since you started, what your sticking point is now, and what you would tell someone who is about to give up. Let me know if Thursday works for you.

Welcome back to The Long Game, the podcast about learning things the slow way. Today, the plateau. Every serious learner hits it, and most of them misread it. They think the plateau means they have stopped. It does not. It means the easy gains are over. When you start, every week brings something new and visible. In the middle, progress becomes small and quiet, a little less hesitation here, one more idiom there. The trap is what people do next. Some quit. Others go back to their comfort zone and use the same twenty sentences forever. The learners who break through do something different. They record themselves, they pinpoint one problem, and they work on that problem, and only that problem, for a month. It is boring, and it works. So if you feel stuck this week, do not add more hours. Choose one thing, and fine-tune it.

First, I say how much of the course I have finished. Then, I say what has changed since I started. After that, I pinpoint my sticking point. Next, I explain how I will work on it with deliberate practice. Finally, I raise the bar for the second half.
